column1: # BATCH 21 — pitch layout most=G high=E mid=G low=E least=G
# Elevated slots are HIGH and LOW. High takes LANE A in all five (it is the trait at
# full pitch and can carry jeopardy). Low takes LANE B in all five — low is a
# withdrawal or a slackening in every entry here, and jeopardy deflates it.
# THE OBJECT IS NAMED IN THE ROW. Not "a decision about staying" but the residency form
# that cannot be posted and flown on in the same week; not "a hardship fund" but the
# eviction date against the run-out meter; not "a big outfit" but the thing that will
# be in every photograph on every wall.
# NEIGHBOURS — taken from src/content/trait-neighbours.tsv, entries read, separations
# written here. No `!` same-batch flags in this batch, but see the note at the end.
#   liminal (bitter-smoked-chickpea) vs footloose (spicy-smoked-green), otherworldly
#     (bitter-smoked-fava), eerie (bitter-smoked-green), hazy (sweet-smoked-butter).
#     Footloose is MOVEMENT — going, the next town by morning, and what it refuses is a
#     commitment to stay. Otherworldly ACTS AGAINST MATERIAL INTEREST on something
#     wordless. Eerie is a signal from somewhere else. Hazy does not know where it is.
#     Liminal is none of those: it knows exactly where it is, which is BETWEEN TWO
#     DEFINED STATES, and it stays there on purpose. It can be entirely stationary and
#     nothing about it is supernatural. So every facet here puts two named states on
#     the page with the reader in the gap.
#   judicious (bitter-boiled-cannellini) vs measured (bitter-boiled-black), careful
#     (bitter-boiled-mung), circumspect (bitter-dried-chickpea), discerning
#     (sour-fermented-cannellini). Careful is about HARM — the third opinion, the
#     cracked seal. Circumspect is wariness of PEOPLE you cannot vouch for. Discerning
#     is TASTE: which is better. Measured is the close one and it is about PACE —
#     refusing to be hurried, "I'll text you in the morning"; it resists pressure.
#     Judicious is the WEIGHING ITSELF: two real options, reasons on both sides, and a
#     verdict produced. So nothing here is unsafe, nobody here is hurrying the reader,
#     and every facet ends in a verdict rather than a delay.
#   challenging (sour-fried-kidney) vs forthright (sour-roasted-edamame), fierce
#     (sour-dried-kidney), inquisitive (bitter-boiled-green), defiant
#     (umami-roasted-fava). Forthright says YOUR OWN thing plainly. Fierce is
#     protective and needs somebody being wronged. Inquisitive asks for the ANSWER'S
#     sake. Defiant goes at an order. Challenging goes at a CLAIM somebody has made and
#     not earned, and the question is a TEST, not a request — the reader may already
#     know the answer. So every facet has a specific claim on the page, no victim, and
#     no authority being disobeyed.
#   flamboyant (spicy-roasted-pinto) vs expansive (umami-roasted-pinto), demonstrative
#     (spicy-roasted-mung), regal (umami-smoked-cannellini), shameless
#     (bitter-roasted-fava). Expansive is ABUNDANCE — the full tour, the itinerary.
#     Demonstrative is FEELING declared. Regal does not perform at all; it holds still
#     and lets them come. Shameless merely does not mind being looked at. Flamboyant
#     GOES OUT AND IS LOOKED AT on purpose, and the display is the gift. So every facet
#     has a chosen visible spectacle in front of named people, and none of them is a
#     declaration of feeling or a rescue.
#   abiding (sweet-dried-black) vs constant (sweet-boiled-black), enduring
#     (umami-dried-navy), lingering (sweet-smoked-navy), steadfast (spicy-smoked-navy).
#     Constant shares the bean AND the flavour and is the dangerous one: it is a
#     REPEATED ACT in ordinary weather — the Saturday doors, the book token — and the
#     cadence is the content. Enduring is the reader's own persistence at a task.
#     Lingering stays attached to what it has LEFT. Steadfast needs the others to have
#     dropped off. Abiding is dried: it needs NO UPKEEP and survives GAPS, and the
#     content is that the bond is intact after a long silence. So no facet here has a
#     cadence, a streak or a comparison with people who stopped.
# WHAT THE NEIGHBOURS FILE DID NOT CATCH — worth recording, because the gap is real.
#   It maps trait to trait. It does not map POLE to trait, and in this batch the
#   collision is exactly there: liminal's LEAST is "planted", which sits on top of
#   abiding's TRAIT, in the same batch. Separated by content, not by axis — planted is
#   ONE ACT OF SETTLING, on a place, choosing a side; abiding is a BOND held across
#   time with a person on the other end. So the chickpea least fixes the reader to a
#   place and has nobody in it to be loyal to, and no black facet is about choosing
#   between two options.
# === bitter-smoked-chickpea — liminal / unmoored / planted
# AXIS: you are between two defined states and comfortable there, and you decline to
#   resolve into either one.
# TITLES: Bean Drift, The Twilight Bean, Beanimbo — all the same idea, the state with
#   no name. The Secret Beanden and There's No Place Like Bean are the inverse: a place
#   that is yours and stays yours.
# OFF-LIMITS: a will-o'-the-wisp that lands nobody ashore; "say how long you're
#   staying"; "one unpacked box is enough to live out of"; "sign something with a date
#   on it"; "a name on a deed carries well"; aubergine ash and half-places.
#   OLD FACETS: six months as a night porter with no daylight; the empty house and the
#     hour on the front-room floor; the level crossing with nothing coming; the border
#     town and "a while yet"; the smallholding with forty years of your father in it.
#     So no night shift, no moving-out floor, no level crossing, no border town, no
#     family land.
#   QUESTION owns: the barbecue where the old players and this year's team have split,
#     and standing between the two of them. No facet is the reader between two GROUPS.
bitter-smoked-chickpea
bitter-smoked-chickpea

bitter-smoked-chickpea
# === bitter-boiled-cannellini — judicious / overcautious / rash
# AXIS: two real options with reasons on both sides, and you weigh them properly before
#   you say which — the weighing takes the time it takes and it ends in a verdict.
# TITLES: Waiting for Beandot is the excess, weighing with nothing arriving. 12 Angry
#   Beans is one holdout taking the room through it properly. Rebel Without a Bean and
#   Thelma & Beanise are the inverse — the move made before any of it is thought about.
# OFF-LIMITS: an eagle owl waiting all night for one kill; "decide it properly and
#   once"; "most decisions keep a day"; "decide the small ones on the spot"; "first to
#   move often takes it"; clear broth and careful salt, a pot that decides late.
#   OLD FACETS: the bridge measured a third time from the other bank; the basket with
#     one mushroom that might be a blusher; the house auction going past the number;
#     the chip pan and the tea towel; the slip road and the lorry on the inside. So no
#     surveying, no foraging, no auction bidding, no kitchen fire, no motorway.
#   QUESTION owns: whether a friend should put an offer in on a house she has seen once.
bitter-boiled-cannellini
bitter-boiled-cannellini
# LANE A — there is enough for one of the two applications, the money goes today, and the other person gets told no.
bitter-boiled-cannellini

# LANE B — how the bunker works: the dormitories, the filtration plant, the room where the list of names was kept.
bitter-boiled-cannellini
# === sour-fried-kidney — challenging / belligerent / acquiescent
# AXIS: somebody states a thing they have not earned, and you make them back it up,
#   there and then.
# TITLES: Roadbean and The Beantlet are both a claim taken apart in front of people.
#   The Beanenger is the small version — whose rule is that? As You Bean and Whatever
#   You Say, Bean are the inverse: it goes through unchallenged.
# OFF-LIMITS: a magpie mobbing a hawk twice its size; "argue with everything and the
#   good argument gets missed"; "the challenge is worth making once"; "let it stand
#   this time"; "agreement gets more done than combat"; tamarind chutney and raised
#   stakes.
#   OLD FACETS: the honey trader and which valley; the book group and the page where it
#     cheats; the driving instructor and whose rule that is; the pub quiz answer wrong
#     on the board; the man with a theory about the buses. So no market stall, no book
#     group, no driving lesson, no pub quiz, and the half-invented-theory shape is spent.
#   QUESTION owns: the work lunch and the trains being better before they were sold off.
sour-fried-kidney
sour-fried-kidney
# LANE A — the vote is taken tonight and a permission, once it is granted, is granted.
sour-fried-kidney
sour-fried-kidney
# LANE B — behind the gallery: the trays, the accession numbers, the things that are not on show.
sour-fried-kidney
# === spicy-roasted-pinto — flamboyant / garish / muted
# AXIS: you turn up as a spectacle on purpose, where people will see it, and the
#   display is the thing you are giving them.
# TITLES: Glitter and Be Bean, Peabean, Bean That Jazz — the turn taken in public.
#   Beanet Please and Shades of Bean are the inverse, and both are about being
#   deliberately unseen.
# OFF-LIMITS: a mandarin duck painted like nothing else on the water; "bright enough
#   and nobody sees what's underneath"; "colour lifts an ordinary day"; "tone it down
#   tonight"; "muted things last longer in the eye"; guajillo and a tray dressing for
#   an audience.
#   OLD FACETS: the coat and the sound effects at somebody else's wedding; the bird of
#     paradise in the bus shelter; the acted-out quiz round; the grey coat on a
#     midweek occasion; going in quietly and leaving before the speeches. THE COAT IS
#     SPENT — no facet in this entry uses one.
#   QUESTION owns: film night on a Tuesday, eight people, and the good coat.
spicy-roasted-pinto
spicy-roasted-pinto
# LANE A — it is in every photograph, on every wall, for the rest of all their lives.
spicy-roasted-pinto
spicy-roasted-pinto
# LANE B — you have been shown the gimmick, the table and how the trick is actually done.
spicy-roasted-pinto
# === sweet-dried-black — abiding / immutable / fleeting
# AXIS: what you have with somebody does not weaken with time or silence, and it needs
#   no keeping up — after years of nothing it is exactly where it was.
# TITLES: Beans Are Forever and Abide With Bean are the thing intact across the gap.
#   Beans in the Wind and Bean Too Soon are the inverse — something allowed to be
#   short, and finished.
# OFF-LIMITS: a tortoise outliving everybody who fed it; "a view that never changes
#   stops being a view"; "old friendships need less upkeep than people think"; "let one
#   thing end properly"; "short things can be complete"; brittle and brown sugar, what
#   sets here not unsetting.
#   OLD FACETS: twenty-two years of letters answered about a third; the decade with no
#     contact and the ring out of nowhere; flowers on the same grave by the long way
#     round; the group going quiet over a year; somebody in town you tell you are not
#     free. So no letter streak, no call from nowhere, no grave, no group going quiet.
#   QUESTION owns: somebody from fifteen years ago getting in touch out of nowhere —
#     so no facet here is the reader receiving contact after a long silence.
sweet-dried-black

# Written last, on the text in the entry files, after the linter and after the six
# fixes below. Nothing has been touched since.
# SIX FAULTS FOUND BY THIS READ. Three were referent breaks and three were POLE NEEDS
# — the line parsed perfectly and had stopped proving its own pole. All re-read below
# on the new text.
#   chickpea high — POLE NEEDS. Nothing on the page said the residency was UNRESOLVED
#     rather than merely deprioritised, so "you get on the plane" read as choosing a
#     wedding over paperwork, which is not liminal at all. Added "on the wrong sort of
#     visa": nine years, still not settled either way.
#   chickpea low — ACT NEEDS. "You take the Tuesday" and no Tuesday anywhere on the
#     page. The rota now has nobody at all on Tuesdays, and the offer is "a morning of
#     your own" so the reader is the one who names the day.
#   cannellini low — POLE NEEDS. Nothing said the commitment was unknown, so signing
#     read as keen rather than unweighed, and the entry's whole axis is the weighing.
#     The form now does not say what it involves.
#   kidney least — "the thing you did" is a placeholder standing in for the content,
#     which is the fault the vagueness rule exists for. Now: he got underneath and
#     found the split hose.
#   pinto high — "the brightest thing in that room" and the page never named a room.
#     The friend is now getting married in the first clause.
#   pinto least — "one ticket for the four o'clock" never says what of. Now a showing.
# LINTER FLAGS LEFT STANDING — the rule, not the prose. Same three as batch 20.
#   "median N, outside 24-48" on all five (54-63). 61 of 190 written entries trip this,
#     batch 19 and 20 included; the band was calibrated on 64 early entries and the
#     house style has moved longer since.
#   BATCH "You tell" 9% and shape D-beats 38%. Corpus-wide totals, both already over
#     before this batch. Five of the 25 acts here use "You tell"; the rest were drafted
#     onto other verbs (make him read, put your name on, wear it, take the Tuesday,
#     laugh in the right place, buy one ticket, put the box in the car).
# --- bitter-smoked-chickpea ---
# MOST
#  ON THE PAGE: you have been in your parents' caravan on the drive since the flat fell
#    through in the spring; you have not given anybody a new address since; your mum
#    says the caravan is promised to your uncle at the end of the month; there is the
#    back room inside if you want it.
#  THE ACT NEEDS: your mum (stated) · your uncle (stated) · holding off, meaning the
#    promise on the caravan (stated).
#  THE POLE NEEDS: excess, because a real room is on the page and refused in favour of
#    the drive, and the no-new-address line says the in-between has become the state
#    rather than a stage. RESIST: you take the back room.
# HIGH
#  ON THE PAGE: nine years in the same country on the wrong sort of visa; the residency
#    form has to go in the post today with your passport inside; that means not flying
#    for four months; your brother is getting married at the weekend; you are at the gate.
#  THE ACT NEEDS: the plane (the gate, stated) · the form (stated).
#  THE POLE NEEDS: the wrong sort of visa across nine years is what makes this the
#    unresolved state rather than a preference — without it the facet was choosing a
#    wedding, and it was the third list that caught that. RESIST: you post the form and
#    miss the wedding. LANE A holds: the four-month window shuts behind the plane.
# MID
#  ON THE PAGE: you have done the beginners' pottery course twice; the beginners' room
#    is where you like being; nobody in it expects anything of you; the tutor has put
#    you on the intermediate list for the autumn.
#  THE ACT NEEDS: the tutor (stated) · the beginners' course (stated).
#  THE POLE NEEDS: low expression — one small refusal to graduate out of the
#    in-between, with the reason ("nobody expects anything of you") stated rather than
#    implied. RESIST: you go up to intermediate.
# LOW
#  ON THE PAGE: you turn up at the sanctuary when you feel like it; the woman who runs
#    it has taken you through the back; which dogs are on what; who holds keys; a rota
#    with three names on it and nobody at all on Tuesdays; she asks whether you would
#    take a set of keys and a morning of your own.
#  THE ACT NEEDS: the Tuesday (now stated) · the morning being taken (stated).
#  THE POLE NEEDS: planted-lite — the reader fixes themselves to one slot on a rota
#    that had a hole in it. RESIST: you carry on turning up when you feel like it.
#    LANE B holds: keys, medication and a three-name rota are how the place runs.
# LEAST
#  ON THE PAGE: two years with her; you have lived out of a bag between her place and
#    your room in the shared house; neither of you has ever said which one you actually
#    live in; she has cleared out two drawers and told you they are yours.
#  THE ACT NEEDS: the room at the other place (the shared house, stated).
#  THE POLE NEEDS: the inverse fully taken — the in-between is named outright on the
#    page, so giving the room up is the vote and not just a tidy-up. RESIST: you keep
#    the room.
# --- bitter-boiled-cannellini ---
# MOST
#  ON THE PAGE: two bikes; one is two hundred more with the better frame; you have been
#    saving for this since the spring; the man says there is one left of each and he
#    will hold either of them until closing.
#  THE ACT NEEDS: the shop (stated) · the two bikes (stated).
#  THE POLE NEEDS: excess, and the evidence is that nobody is hurrying — he has offered
#    to hold them, which keeps it off measured — and the reader still cannot land it
#    while one of each is left. RESIST: you buy one of them.
# HIGH
#  ON THE PAGE: you are one of three on the hardship panel; enough left for one of two
#    applications; a woman three weeks behind with an eviction date; a man whose meter
#    has run out with two children; the other two have split; it comes down to you; the
#    money goes today.
#  THE ACT NEEDS: the woman (stated) · the eviction date (stated).
#  THE POLE NEEDS: the trait rather than the excess, because a verdict is actually
#    produced — two options, reasons on both sides, and a decision. RESIST: you give it
#    to the meter. LANE A holds: the money goes once and the other one gets told no.
# MID
#  ON THE PAGE: the dentist says the tooth can have a filling today for eighty pounds
#    or a crown in three weeks for four hundred; either is perfectly defensible; he has
#    the drill in his hand; there are people after you.
#  THE ACT NEEDS: the dentist (stated) · the tooth (stated).
#  THE POLE NEEDS: "either is perfectly defensible" is doing the separation work — with
#    nothing unsafe on the page this is judgement, not care. RESIST: you tell him to do
#    the filling.
# LOW
#  ON THE PAGE: the bunker tour takes the nine of you through the dormitories, the
#    filtration plant and the room where the list of names was kept; the guide says
#    they are short of volunteer guides; there is a form on the table that does not say
#    what it involves.
#  THE ACT NEEDS: the form (stated).
#  THE POLE NEEDS: rash-lite, and it needs the form to be uninformative — otherwise
#    signing is enthusiasm rather than the absence of weighing, which is the pole.
#    RESIST: you ask what it involves first. LANE B holds: the filtration plant and the
#    list of names are how the place worked.
# LEAST
#  ON THE PAGE: your friend has gone in to put five pounds on; you came in with her;
#    the man ahead of you is telling the counter about a horse in the four o'clock.
#  THE ACT NEEDS: the horse (stated) · its name (the horse is stated; the reader
#    supplies liking it).
#  THE POLE NEEDS: the inverse fully — fifty against her five, on an overheard tip, for
#    a reason that is not a reason. RESIST: you put a fiver on, or nothing.
# --- sour-fried-kidney ---
# MOST
#  ON THE PAGE: a woman two chairs along says her cousin was seen in twenty minutes at
#    the walk-in centre across town and this place is a disgrace; she is waiting to be
#    called for a scan; her hands have not been still since you sat down.
#  THE ACT NEEDS: her (stated) · her cousin (stated).
#  THE POLE NEEDS: belligerent, and the evidence is the scan and the hands — she is
#    frightened, she is not anybody's opponent, the claim costs nothing, and the reader
#    goes at it anyway. RESIST: you let her have it.
# HIGH
#  ON THE PAGE: the developer's man tells the meeting the ecology survey found no bats
#    in the barn; you have the survey open in front of you at the line saying the roof
#    was never accessed; they vote at the end of the night; a permission once granted
#    is granted.
#  THE ACT NEEDS: him (stated) · the paragraph, meaning the line in the survey (stated).
#  THE POLE NEEDS: a specific claim, unearned, tested on the spot, with the reader
#    holding the evidence — and no authority being disobeyed, which keeps it off
#    defiant. RESIST: you let it go to the vote. LANE A holds: a permission does not
#    come back.
# MID
#  ON THE PAGE: somebody at your table says the recycling all goes in the same lorry as
#    everything else; the four of them nod along at it.
#  THE ACT NEEDS: him (stated).
#  THE POLE NEEDS: low expression — one challenge, made once, on a claim of no
#    consequence, and it is a test rather than a question. RESIST: you nod along too.
# LOW
#  ON THE PAGE: a friend has got you into the store rooms behind the gallery; the
#    trays, the accession numbers, the things that never go on show; the curator pulls
#    out a drawer and says the brooch in it came off a wreck; you know that was
#    disproved years ago.
#  THE ACT NEEDS: the curator (stated) · the brooch (stated) · the drawer (stated).
#  THE POLE NEEDS: acquiescent-lite, and it needs the reader to have both the claim and
#    the knowledge on the page so the declining is legible as a choice. RESIST: you
#    tell her it was disproved. LANE B holds: the trays and the accession numbers are
#    the inside of the place.
# LEAST
#  ON THE PAGE: your friend is telling the six of them about the night the van broke
#    down; you were there; in his version it is him who got underneath and found the
#    split hose.
#  THE ACT NEEDS: him (stated) · the story (stated) · the right place in it (stated).
#  THE POLE NEEDS: the inverse fully — first-hand standing to knock it down, and the
#    reader not only lets it through but helps it along. RESIST: you say it was you
#    under the van.
# --- spicy-roasted-pinto ---
# MOST
#  ON THE PAGE: your friend is collecting on the pavement outside the shops for the
#    hospice her mum was in; she has a bucket and a laminated sign; you have come with
#    a costume, a speaker and twenty minutes of material; she has asked you twice to
#    just rattle the bucket today.
#  THE ACT NEEDS: the speaker (stated).
#  THE POLE NEEDS: garish, and all three pieces of evidence are on the page — the
#    occasion is her mother's hospice, she has asked twice, and the display takes her
#    day off her. RESIST: you rattle the bucket.
# HIGH
#  ON THE PAGE: your oldest friend is getting married; she said wear what you like;
#    what you have had made will be the brightest thing in that room by a distance; she
#    saw it on the hanger and said, carefully, that this was a lot; every photograph on
#    every wall in her family will have it in, for good.
#  THE ACT NEEDS: it, meaning what you had made (stated) · the room (now stated as the
#    wedding).
#  THE POLE NEEDS: the trait not the excess, because permission was actually given —
#    "wear what you like" — and the price is permanence rather than offence. RESIST:
#    you wear something else. LANE A holds: the photographs do not come down.
# MID
#  ON THE PAGE: six of you have a cottage for the weekend; it is nobody's birthday; the
#    plan for tonight is a takeaway and cards; you have a case of costumes in the boot
#    that nobody asked for.
#  THE ACT NEEDS: the costumes (stated) · the sofa (a cottage, stated).
#  THE POLE NEEDS: low expression — the occasion is deliberately nothing, so putting
#    them out is the whole of the display. RESIST: they stay in the boot.
# LOW
#  ON THE PAGE: your friend knows the magician; he has taken you round the back before
#    the second half; the table, the gimmick, the whole of how the trick is done; he
#    says he needs somebody up out of the seats and would rather it were you than a
#    stranger.
#  THE ACT NEEDS: the magician (stated) · somebody else, meaning the seats (stated).
#  THE POLE NEEDS: muted-lite, and it needs the role to be offered on a plate and named
#    so that declining is a vote and not a blank. RESIST: you go up. LANE B holds: you
#    have been shown how the trick works.
# LEAST
#  ON THE PAGE: every year you have booked a room and asked thirty people; every year
#    they have come; this one you have booked nothing and told nobody.
#  THE ACT NEEDS: the ticket (stated) · the showing (now stated).
#  THE POLE NEEDS: the room and the thirty people are what make one ticket a choice
#    rather than a quiet life. RESIST: you book the room again.
# --- sweet-dried-black ---
# MOST
#  ON THE PAGE: since school the four of you have had it that whoever is nearest goes,
#    whatever has happened and whatever time of night; he has three under five now; he
#    has asked to be taken off.
#  THE ACT NEEDS: him (stated) · it, meaning the arrangement (stated).
#  THE POLE NEEDS: immutable — he has asked, with a reason on the page, and the thing
#    is still not allowed to change. There is no cadence and no repeated act in it,
#    which is what keeps it off constant. RESIST: you take him off.
# HIGH
#  ON THE PAGE: his sister is going round the room asking what he would have wanted
#    played; nobody can agree; you and he were inseparable until you were twenty-two
#    and then did not speak for eleven years; the order of service goes to the printer
#    tonight.
#  THE ACT NEEDS: the sister (stated) · the song (stated) · him telling you at twenty
#    (the friendship at that age is stated).
#  THE POLE NEEDS: the eleven years of nothing is the evidence — the bond needed no
#    upkeep and the thing he said survived it intact. RESIST: you say you would not
#    know any more. LANE A holds: it prints tonight and that room never assembles again.
# MID
#  ON THE PAGE: you shared a flat with her for two years; you have not seen her since;
#    she is three seats up on the same bus with four stops to go; her brother lost two
#    fingers in a machine that winter.
#  THE ACT NEEDS: her (stated) · her brother (stated) · his hand (stated).
#  THE POLE NEEDS: low expression — the detail survived years of nothing, and going
#    straight to it rather than to pleasantries is the whole of the vote. RESIST: you
#    do the four stops on how work is going.
# LOW
#  ON THE PAGE: the guide takes the ten of you off the public route; how the bones were
#    stacked; which families paid for the privilege; you spend the whole two hours
#    talking to the woman next to you; at the top she gets her phone out to swap numbers.
#  THE ACT NEEDS: her (stated) · the two hours (stated).
#  THE POLE NEEDS: fleeting-lite, and the declined act is on the page as her phone
#    coming out, so letting it be complete is a real vote. RESIST: you get your phone
#    out too. LANE B holds: the route off the public route is the inside of the place.
# LEAST
#  ON THE PAGE: the box in the loft is ten years of one friendship — the photographs,
